articles.title: Asian Games Medal Tally: Why India dropped out of top 10 despite winning seven more medals
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India added seven more medals to its Asian Games 2026 tally on Sunday, but the haul was not enough to keep the country inside the top 10 of the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India added seven more medals to its Asian Games 2026 tally on Sunday, but the haul was not enough to keep the country inside the top 10 of the medal standings.India ended Day 8 with 37 medals — four gold, 16 silver and 17 bronze — but slipped from 10th to 12th position. The drop came despite the sizeable medal haul because India did not add a gold, while countries above it continued to accumulate gold medals and increase their overall totals.China continued to dominate the Games after crossing the 200-medal mark, with 119 gold, 48 silver and 38 bronze for 205 medals. Japan and South Korea remained second and third.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleSeven medals, but no gold for IndiaIndia's seven medals on Sunday included two silver from squash and five from athletics.Parul Chaudhary produced one of the day's standout performances, breaking her personal best to win bronze in the women's 3000m steeplechase. She clocked 9:08.67, a new national record, to claim her second Asian Games steeplechase medal after winning silver at Hangzhou in 2023.Bahrain's Winfred Yavi won gold in 9:04.36, while Kazakhstan's Norah Jeruto Tanui took silver. India's Ankita finished fourth in a personal-best 9:19.24.Sarvesh Kushare and Ancy Sojan also won silver medals after leading their respective finals for significant periods. Sarvesh cleared 2.25m but finished second to Chinese Taipei's Chao Hsuan-Fu, while Ancy's 6.53m was bettered by China's Huang Yingying, who produced 6.55m with her final attempt.Harita Bhadra had earlier won bronze in the women's 200m in 23.20 seconds, edging Japan's Ido Abigeirufuka by 0.01 seconds.Tejaswin Shankar completed India's athletics haul with bronze in the decathlon. He won the final event, the 1500m, in 4:33.09 and finished with 7,934 points. Japan's Yuma Maruyama won gold with 8,123 points.Squash misses gold, boxing adds three assured medalsIndia's wait for a squash singles gold continued as both Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh lost their finals to Malaysian opponents. Sivasangari Subramaniam beat Anahat 11-4, 11-4, 11-7, while Ng Eain Yow defeated Abhay 11-9, 11-5, 11-5.Anahat's silver was historic as she became the first Indian woman to reach an Asian Games squash singles final.India's medal prospects received a boost in boxing, with Parveen Hooda, Ankush Panghal and Narender all reaching the semifinals and assuring themselves medals.The day's results underline the medal-table challenge: India won seven more medals but added no gold, while countries above it continued to build their gold-medal totals. articles.title: Gleyber Torres' two-year run with Tigers comes to frustrating end
articles.summary: After making the All-Star team in 2025, persistent oblique issues this season kept free-agent-to-be Torres from playing up to his own high standards.
articles.body:
DETROIT — Gleyber Torres at least has kept his sense of humor through it all.

This has been a rough year for him, health-wise and otherwise, and that it has come in a contract year only compounds the disappointment.

His season and probably his Tigers' tenure, ended Tuesday, Sept. 22. He's not played since and he wasn't expected to play in the finale Sunday. And when he was asked his thoughts on his pending free agency, he gave a wry smile.

"I know my agent will have to work hard," he said. "I don't do too much this year. I do a little bit. Hopefully he does the job and gets me something good."

Torres will be going into his age-30 season. And after going through sports hernia surgery last winter , he's grinded through a season where he was put on the injured list twice with oblique strains.

"Unfortunately, this season has been awful," he said. "Twice injured. I don't feel like I performed like I am used to performing. Last year with the injury, this year with the injury, it never let me play like I can play. It sucks. I wanted to play really good coming off of last year when I helped the team a lot. This year, I didn't do much."

While he played a career-low 96 games and had a career-low 420 plate appearances (not counting the COVID season of 2020), he was still a 2-WAR player.

"I didn't feel as strong as I did last year," he said. "I tried to play a different way and I tried to push myself a little more, but I never felt good. For sure I kept playing because I have to play. But for myself, I never felt strong."

His slash-line wasn't far off his career norms — .260/.364/.363 with a .727 OPS — but, except for a few stretches, he wasn't as impactful has he was last season when he was the American League's starting second baseman in the All-Star game.

"I did all I could do to be healthy and help the team," he said. "It is what it is. Injuries suck, but they are part of the game. I will have the offseason to fix a couple of things and come back even stronger than ever and we'll see where I'm going to be next year."

He accepted the Tigers' qualifying offer last winter and earned $22.05 million this season. He understands that the odds of making more than that or getting a long-term contract this offseason, especially with the pending labor uncertainty, are long.

"I've had a lot of conversations with my agent," he said. "December is going to be different than it's been in the past but we don't know what it's going to be like. Injured twice, like, you know how the business is. We'll see. Hopefully I can get a deal I deserve."

He did not rule out the possibility of re-signing with the Tigers, but he sees the influx of young infielders coming up, like Hao-Yu Lee and Max Anderson, one of the few higher-level prospects who didn't debut this season.

"My time here was great," he said. "I like this group. I like the organization. I've enjoyed all of my teammates. It's a special group and I'm glad I got to play here. I will always be grateful for the opportunity here. Who knows about next year, but speaking in the present, it was good. The people here treated me like a brother from the beginning."

articles.title: Chiefs Announce Sudden Chamarri Conner Decision Hours Before Dolphins Game
articles.summary: The Chiefs announced a sudden Chamarri Conner decision just hours before their game against the Dolphins, putting the safety in focus. The post Chiefs Announ...
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs safety Chamarri Conner will not suit up Sunday in Miami , sidelined for a third straight week by the same knee that has trailed him through the first quarter of the 2026 season.

The Kansas City Chiefs safety went from doubtful to out with only about two hours to go before kickoff Sunday, leaving a secondary that has already logged two games without him to lean once more on a pair of backups against a Dolphins team still in search of its first win.

Conner was limited in practice all three days last week, according to the Chiefs' official injury report, before Kansas City tagged him doubtful Friday. Coach Andy Reid framed the workload as progress.

"He's making progress, so he's up practicing and moving around," Reid said Friday, as quoted by Arrowhead Pride , describing Conner's status heading into the weekend. The club made it official Sunday morning, ruling teh 26-year-old out for the Dolphins game. His next chance to return comes Oct. 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders .

Kansas City Chiefs' Chamarri Conner Injury Timeline

Conner has yet to play a snap in 2026. He sat out the opener against Denver and Week 2 against Indianapolis with the same knee, marking his third consecutive missed game to start the year. It is not his first extended absence. He also missed the final two weeks of 2024 with a concussion.

Born July 11, 2000, in Jacksonville, Florida, Conner starred at multiple positions in the secondary at Virginia Tech before Kansas City traded up with Minnesota to grab him in the fourth round, 119th overall, in the 2023 NFL Draft. He signed a four-year, $4.59 million rookie contract , according to Over The Cap, and has since collected a Super Bowl LVIII ring.

The safety's workload ballooned last season, when he played nearly every defensive snap and racked up a career-high 117 tackles. He has 230 tackles across three NFL seasons to go with four interceptions and three forced fumbles, one of which he returned for a touchdown against Cincinnati in 2024.

Safeties Jaden Hicks and Alohi Gilman have played every defensive snap through two games and will start again Sunday, with rookie Xavier Nwankpa in reserve. Hicks has already turned heads, posting 10 tackles in Kansas City's overtime win over Indianapolis, a workload that will only continue to grow as long as Conner remains sidelined.

Losing Conner costs the Chiefs their most versatile piece in the secondary, a safety who can play in the box, cover the slot and line up as a hybrid nickel. Without him, Kansas City may lean harder on cornerback Mansoor Delane to fill that role. Reid sounded confident Friday about Delane's availability.

"Good chance, yeah," Reid said, as quoted by Chiefs On SI , when asked if Delane would play against Miami.

Chris Jones and L'Jarius Sneed each carry no game-day designation despite limited practice work, and left tackle Josh Simmons is out for a third straight week with a training-camp back injury. The rest of Kansas City's roster, including quarterback Patrick Mahomes , is otherwise healthy.

Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's unit has already survived two full games without Conner, and Miami's offense has managed just 13 points per game so far. The real question hovering over Kansas City's secondary isn't whether it can cover for one missing piece. It's whether Hicks keeps holding up as an every-down starter rather than the rotational piece he was a year ago.

articles.title: Bills Get D.J. Moore Injury News Hours Before Chargers Game
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills get great injury news on $110 million WR before Week 3 game against Los Angeles Chargers. The post Bills Get D.J. Moore Injury News Hours Befor...
articles.body:
While most teams seem like battering rams for bad injury news, the unbeaten Buffalo Bills flipped the script on Sunday ahead of a Week 3 home game against the Los Angeles Chargers .

First, the Bills found out that wide receiver Keon Coleman would play after a week of doubt.

"Bills WR D.J. Moore , listed as questionable for today due to a shoulder injury, is expected to play vs. the Chargers, per source," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account.

" DJ Moore will be ACTIVE as I anticipated," Dr. Jesse Morse wrote on his official X account. "He's a DAWG, but will be at moderate risk of reinjury."

Moore had 5 receptions for 100 yards and 1 touchdown in a Week 1 win over the Houston Texans but was hurt early in a Week 2 win over the Detroit Lions .

Massive Praise for Moore After Opening Win

Sports Illustrated's Eva Geithem called Moore the NFL's "Top Offseason Addition" after his sparkling Week 1 debut.

"After they had struggled in recent matchups against the Texans, the Bills' offense was explosive against Houston on Sunday, racking up 36 points and 409 yards of offense," Geithem wrote on September 15. "One reason for the improvement? The addition of D.J. Moore. the Bills' prior lack of top-end receivers made it hard for them to challenge the Texans' defense, but with Moore—and tight end Dalton Kincaid being healthy—they were able to create big plays in the passing game and score 36 points. Case in point, Moore averaged 20 yards per catch as he hauled in five passes for 100 yards and a touchdown. The Bills had to pay a steep trade price to land Moore (a second-round pick for Moore and a fifth), but if he continues to have this positive of an impact on the passing game, it will be well worth the cost."

articles.title: Washington football plummets out of US LBM Coaches Poll
articles.summary: The Washington Huskies took a massive tumble down the US LBM Coaches Poll following a 27-24 loss to Minnesota.
articles.body:
Following a 27-24 loss to the Minnesota Golden Gophers, the Washington Huskies won't be sniffing the top 25 of the US LBM Coaches Poll for a while.

After beginning Big Ten play as the No. 23 team in the country, Jedd Fisch's team had a golden opportunity to move up the rankings and take advantage of some turmoil around the Big Ten, with three ranked teams in the conference losing. USC fell at home to Oregon, while Michigan suffered a last-second loss in the Big House to Iowa , and Wisconsin went on the road to take down Penn State.

However, Fisch's team looked largely unprepared to deal with coach P.J. Fleck's squad, as the Huskies went down 14-0 in the first quarter following an early interception from Demond Williams Jr. and another slow start from the offense. The end result? 20 points in the poll.

In a game full of self-inflicted blunders and mismanagement from the Huskies, one stood out above the rest. With UW down 27-17 with around 2:30 to play, wide receiver Chris Lawson picked up a first down and got out of bounds. That stopped the clock to move the chains, but the Huskies chose not to go up-tempo and instead made a late substitution, allowing Minnesota to do the same as the clock wound all the way down to the two-minute timeout, wasting a clock stoppage for Washington.

"I thought there was a point there that Chris got knocked out of bounds, and it was a first down. So then they were resetting the chains, so they stopped the clock on the first down. And then we wanted to get a touchdown," Fisch said after the game.

"We wanted to get a certain red zone play in. And we wound up subbing, and the sub came in way too late. And with that, then they got to hold another 10 seconds. So that's my fault. There was a certain personnel group that I wanted in the game for that play, so we wound up having to call it after the two-minute warning."

Now, the Huskies will have to head down to Los Angeles to face off with the No. 18 Trojans , who dropped six spots after their loss to the Ducks. Here's how the top 25 shaped up.

articles.title: Patriots vs. Jaguars live updates: Score, news, discussion from NFL Week 3
articles.summary: The Patriots are taking on the Jaguars in Week 3 of the NFL regular season.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots are entering the third week of the 2026 NFL regular season trying to end a disappointing streak. They have started every one of their last five campaigns with a 1-2 record.

In order to prevent the same from happening and improve to 2-1 on the year for the first time since their Cam Newton-led 2020 campaign, the Patriots will need to beat another 1-1 squad on the road: the Jacksonville Jaguars , who won their season opener before dropping last Sunday's game in Denver .

The Patriots, meanwhile, are trending in an opposite direction based on an admittedly small two-game sample size: they lost the NFL opener before rebounding with a win over the Steelers one week ago. Can they make it two in a row? Let's find out together.

Welcome to our Patriots-Jaguars live tracker and community discussion.

Sunday, Sept. 27, 1 p.m. ET | EverBank Stadium (Jacksonville, FL) | Broadcast information | Inactives | Game day roster | Weather forecast

The Patriots won the toss and deferred, putting their defense on the field to start things off. A pair of Jacksonville penalties started them off moving backwards, before Trevor Lawrence 's attempt to pick up a 3rd-and-8 with his legs was stopped short.

New England 's offense started with two short gains by Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson to set up an opening 3rd-and-5. Forced to use a timeout to avoid a delay of game, Maye then connected with Mack Hollins for a 21-yard gain to move across midfield. The following third-down saw Maye's pass over the middle to Hunter Henry fall incomplete forcing a punt.

Jaguars' running back Bhaysul Tuten picked up their first first-down of the day getting around the left edge on the ground. New England's defense then buckled down, as a big third-down hit by Christian Gonzalez following a short completion led to a punt.

Maye found a pair of first downs with his legs and back to Mack Hollins to again move the offense across midfield. They're facing a 3rd-and-2, Stevenson just picked up enough on the ground to move the chains. As Maye then looked to push it downfield, the ball slipped out of his hand during his throwing motion which led to the Jaguars recovering the fumble.

An 18-yard completion to Parker Washington on third-down got the Jaguars offense on the move before the run game set them up just outside the red zone. Then inside the red zone, Lawrence found Josh Cameron over the middle for a 12-yard touchdown. | Patriots 0 : 7 Jaguars

Two short gains from TreVeyon Henderson set the Patriots up with a 3rd-and-3, where Maye looked to escape up the pocket and move the chains himself but was brought down for a 0-yard sack.

The Patriots defense generated a much needed turnover, as tight coverage from Jaylen Reed led to a deflected pass which Marcus Jones intercepted.

New England took over at the 21-yard line following the interception. Maye took off and found the end zone with his legs but the score was negated due to a holding call on Morgan Moses . The unit continued to go backwards as Romeo Doubs was called for offensive pass interference. A scramble drill double pass from Efton Chism III to Mack Hollins the short completion to Doubs set up a 3rd-and-7, where Maye extended and just missed a completion in the end zone to Hollins. Andy Borregales' 35-yard field goal was then good. | Patriots 3 : 7 Jaguars

After cutting into the Jaguars' lead on the previous drive, the home team fought back on its next possession. Methodically marching 65 yards in nine plays, the defense surrendered a 10-yard touchdown pass to ex-Patriot Jakobi Meyers . | Patriots 3 : 14 Jaguars

Drake Maye and company were in dire need of some momentum on their next drive, and they found it on the second play of the series when Drake Maye hit DeMario Douglas for a gain of 38. The pair nearly connected for another big gain two plays later, but Maye overshot the wideout for an incompletion on 2nd-and-10. Things did not get any better. A defensive holding penalty extended the series on a near-interception, and a Maye fumble on a scramble was recovered by the QB himself. However, he was not that lucky on a 3rd-and-goal from the 2-yard line: trying to hit Efton Chism, he was intercepted in the end zone by Travis Hunter .

Stay on top of every Patriots update and debate every snap with other diehard fans. Game-day discussion is smoother in the SB Nation app.
